hints.title: Duplicate Value Chunk Isolation
hints.text: Elements may now be arbitrary values with duplicates. When an incoming element is smaller than the maximum of an existing chunk, those chunks must merge into one.

hints.title: Chunk Maximum Monotonicity Invariant
hints.text: Maintaining the maximum element of each chunk in an ascending sequence allows merging violated chunks whenever an incoming element is strictly less than preceding maxima.

hints.title: Monotonic Maximum Tracking Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through the array maintaining a list of chunk maximums. If the current element is greater than or equal to the top of the list, append it as a new chunk. Otherwise, preserve the current top maximum, pop all elements strictly greater than the current element, and push back that preserved maximum.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing against sorted copies or prefix-suffix arrays works, but naive nested merging takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A monotonic stack of chunk maximums processes each element in amortized O(1) operations, taking O(N) total time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle arbitrary numbers with duplicates cleanly and explain why merged chunks preserve their original maximum.
